title: Native Weil Hom into a K-injective target inverts source quasi-isomorphisms
statement: Fix a finite field k_0, a prime l different from its characteristic, and a k_0-scheme X. Let W be the native category of pro-etale Weil sheaves of coefficient modules on the geometric fiber of X. Let H be its native internal-Hom bifunctor, with conjugation Weil structure. If a: K -> L is any quasi-isomorphism of integer-indexed cochain complexes in W and I is any K-injective complex in W, the native product-Hom precomposition map Hom_H(L,I) -> Hom_H(K,I) is a quasi-isomorphism. The product Hom has the actual source-library row-sign differential (-1)^p(d_I f - f d_K). No boundedness or monomorphism assumption is imposed. The fixed-pair category is [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], with the geometric site and size conventions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Tag 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined), source-variable case, and Tag 08BJ; agent-formulated native equivariant specialization. The proof uses a flat separator and the signed source-cone calculation rather than localized-site section cohomology.

proof.text: The underlying coefficient sheaves have a flat separator, by the sheaf flat-resolution theorem and its inheritance by internal modules. Compare the old Mod.tensorLeft with the categorical relative tensor using their coequalizer universal properties. If P is flat, Mod.tensorLeft P is exact.

Use symmetry/transposition and the module tensor-Hom adjunction to identify Hom(P,Hom(M,N)) additively and naturally with Hom(M tensor_R P,N). The signed cochain equivalence multiplies the (p,n) component by (-1)^(p*n). If K is acyclic and I K-injective, every cocycle from K tensor_R P to I is a coboundary. Thus every map P to a cycle of Hom(K,I) lifts to the previous degree. Apply the separator property to kernel(d) -> cokernel(previous d); this map vanishes, proving acyclicity.

For any quasi-isomorphism a its cone is acyclic. The signed bifunctor source-cone isomorphism identifies Hom(Cone(a),I) with Cone(Hom(a,I))[-1]. Step 2 and shift stability imply that Cone(Hom(a,I)) is acyclic, and the cone criterion gives the ordinary module Hom quasi-isomorphism.

Forgetting Frobenius is right adjoint to exact integer-orbit induction, so preserves K-injective complexes. It is exact and conservative. Its product comparison gives the chain isomorphism from underlying native Hom to ordinary module Hom; check the differential and source-map square after every product projection. Apply step 3 to the forgotten source map, then reflect quasi-isomorphisms.
